Consolidation must preserve those differences.

ExecutorWakeInbox persists coalesced pending records before acknowledging enqueue, monitors timed waiters and distinguishes consumer-scoped acknowledgement/fast-forward from legacy acknowledgement. Its pending read maps errors to an empty list while stats exposes errors; caller and inherited-finding review are needed before judging that collapse.

CacheHistory and QuotaHistory have identical sample/samples callback bodies, including unavailable sampling returning ok without a new sample. This is a narrow shared bounded-history candidate, not proof their sampling schemas or whole services are interchangeable.

LiveConversation differentiates canonical activation, trusted normalization, invalid sources and restart-unknown snapshots. Provider account transitions carry caller identity, binding authority and events; provider-meter reads preserve unknown accounts and redacted generations.

Opencode slot claims are caller-owned, monitored and limited by ready/active/claimed state. Reserve-stop, attach, visible selection and deselection are different transitions. PaneManager open checks refocus failure and reopens; attach ignores its refocus result. The latter is a follow-up candidate, not a verified user-visible failure in this pass.

Orchestrator and Tmux already delegate to domain modules. Callback count alone does not show missing extraction; evaluating remaining coupling requires tracing state ownership, blocking work and dependencies behind those delegates.

PauseContainment accepts a process group only when it matches the root PID and fences later operations by generation. Release and release_target duplicate a narrow timer-reset transition. ProcessReaper immediately kills late registrations when draining and separates unregister from reap; those ownership rules must survive extraction.

Flush means different things: RunTelemetry.Writer returns ok as a mailbox barrier here; DecisionMetrics.Writer performs Persistence.flush, ProgressRetention exposes do_flush errors and GitHub.Quota calls RequestLog.sync. The callback names do not establish a common durability guarantee.

ControlCenterCache executes loaders in its handler and uses age/event keys. FinancialData.Cache revalidates identity, prunes stale configuration and delegates authorized fetch with from. Shared cache naming must not erase authority or deferred-reply policy.

Webhooks distinguish delivery deduplication, monotonic position advancement, replay and configured delivery modes. Ownership Store uses persistence replies; VoiceSessionLimiter separately counts authority/global capacity and monitors lease owners. Acceptance and persistence helper behavior remain transitive verification work.

reviewed_families.name: handle_info
reviewed_families.coverage: All 501 literal clauses in 96 modules read in bounded source batches. Macro-generated callbacks, producers, delegated helpers, complete task lifecycles and runtime/UI behavior are not certified by this family pass.
reviewed_families.assessment: This family combines GenServer, LiveView and channel handlers. Common noreply syntax spans stale-result rejection, process ownership, durable retry, event projection, rendering and authority revocation; it is not a universal worker abstraction.
constraints: GraphProjection distinguishes demand monitors, reconciliation tasks and in-flight reads; timeouts match attempts and due messages match tokens. TicketDetailCoordinator reconciles configuration before completing tasks. Preserve those fences and pending-work admission, rather than treating every DOWN or task result alike.

ToolCallLedger marks an owner-dead invocation uncertain. Claude telemetry revokes owner capabilities and stops if its listener exits; DisplayTailer marks an inner tailer unavailable but stops normally when its owner dies. Ownership failure has deliberately different consequences.

CoordinationTasks terminates a timed-out task and completes its queue entry; DecisionDispatchTasks first deactivates, terminates, notifies, cleans owner state and dispatches more work. DecisionStore correlates decision/action/attempt results, ignores stale replies and reconciles after coordinator death.

CurrentRunProjections matches source-refresh references and checkpoints carry generations; SnapshotStore checks both task reference and active orchestrator generation before publication. Name-level extraction must preserve rejection of stale results and retained views during incomplete refresh.

SubscriptionStore holds later events behind a stalled event, retries enqueue and eventually resolves via success or dead-letter handling. ExecutorListener checks/rebinds missing routing and replays after reattachment. Cursor/replay semantics require helper review; comments claiming exactly-once are not proven by these handlers.

BranchRefStore persistence retries and ExecutorWakeInbox timed flushes use tokens; inbox waiters cancel monitors/timers on expiry or caller death. Untagged flush and legacy tick messages coexist with fenced variants, so tokenization cannot be assumed universal.

CacheHistory and QuotaHistory share sampling cadence even when unavailable and differ in sample meaning. GitHub and ElevenLabs quota refreshes both monitor asynchronous work and reschedule on DOWN, but GitHub also refreshes broker alerts and separately handles budget-recovery tokens.

IssueLog responds to linked exits by checking registration and resubscribing or stopping when the identity is taken. LauncherWatchdog shuts down on launcher loss. Ignoring unrelated EXIT messages elsewhere is not proof that all exit handling should share one policy.

Opencode Server replies to readiness waiters on port readiness or exit. AttachPool checks the current slot PID before accepting ready; Slot monitors claim owners, probes pane liveness and respawns only after its own failure threshold. The full producer/cleanup paths remain outside this pass.

SessionWriter skips live-stream-covered transcript/alert rows but preserves remote-user and between-turn writes. Its duplicate suppression depends on live_stream_active and fallback writers; merging render paths requires verifying those dependencies, not deleting similar-looking handlers.

Orchestrator already delegates dispatch, retry, comment reconciliation, accounting and controls. Tick/retry tokens, workspace guardian generations and CI result references remain part of those domain contracts. Budget-pause recovery explicitly requests a poll refresh; it is not only a state update.

PauseContainment fences fallback/liveness/reap results by generation and mode. RepoBase matches build/probe identities and distinguishes probe timeout from an idle hold watchdog, which can rearm for a live worker. Liveness does not itself prove useful progress or a bounded build.

RunTelemetry.Sampler prevents overlapping scans, records overlap/failure warnings and matches completion tokens. ProviderMeterRefresh has an independent one-time baseline and watched refresh loop. Shared periodic scheduling must preserve admission, visibility and rescheduling policy.

Financial cache/configuration changes clear entries and pending work; subscription authority clears subscribers; voice and Streamdeck channels stop on changed authority generation. UI helpers must not turn revocation into a cosmetic refresh.

LiveViews often delegate common AwaitingCommands handlers already. StreamdeckLive has three identical selected-ticket log refresh paths that are a narrow local consolidation candidate, while channel transcript/alert/control payloads differ. TranscriptRelay coalesces to the latest event but forwards alerts/control immediately; this is not a lossless transcript queue.

Catch-all noreply clauses, no-op notification branches and similarly named DOWN handlers are protocol handling, not independently counted duplication defects. Source reading does not establish visual correctness, full transitive recovery or measured savings.

DecisionSanitizer copies allowed fields; ExecutorWakeProjection excludes executor topics and derives typed, trusted wake data. These trust boundaries differ from ordinary layout assembly.

CacheInspector preserves unavailable separately from empty and counts elision. GroupedScopes needs pricing/relationships. Timeline clamps elided gaps; StreamDeckGrid ranks/paginates, while StreamdeckLogs joins transcript/events and pins live position.
Two bodyless declarations are counted. Helper correctness, accounting truth and rendered behavior are not certified.

reviewed_families.name: datetime

constraints: Lifecycle, Member, RootSummary, TicketContextPresenter, ConversationDrawer.Presenter and ProviderMetersPresenter accept DateTime structs and otherwise nil. This repeated two-clause policy is a narrow candidate for a named DateTime-only helper.

reviewed_families.name: reset
reviewed_families.assessment: Reset ranges from ANSI output and process-table clearing to durable budget deletion and authority-sensitive UI state changes.
constraints: DispatchBudgetStore reads before deleting a lifetime and propagates read/write failures. BranchRefStore resets through its process. BrokerTimeout swallows process-unavailable failures; ETS resets differ in existence checks and error handling.

ReadCache resets entries/markers and metrics together; CredentialHeadroom clears two tables. ResourceStore clears its table through a wrapper. Shared empty-state naming does not prove equal persistence or notification requirements.
StartupClaimReconciler.BootMarker erases a persistent-term marker; TrackedSet normalizes identifiers before replacing state. Renderer.Style simply returns an ANSI reset sequence.

reviewed_families.name: schedule

reviewed_families.name: evaluate
reviewed_families.assessment: Evaluation spans pure classification, configuration analysis, state transitions and effectful monitoring.
constraints: CIReadiness compares required check identities and app integrations against PR workflows. GitHubCIPoller gives incomplete signals precedence over failure and requires observed CI before passed; neither is a generic Boolean readiness check.

Outcome.SourceState preserves run matching, repository availability, source health, truncation and freshness reasons. DecisionAuthority evaluates all policy checks; DecisionStore distinguishes fresh from versioned decisions.

BuildGateHoldMonitor emits new/resolved alerts; SaturationSentinel reads clock/load and records diagnostics; SupervisionHealth reconciles monitors and notifies changes. An evaluate name is not a pure-function guarantee.

CLI dispatches parsed options with injected runtime dependencies. PRHealthScanner drops unusable PR numbers before classification; BrokerTimeout prunes events before degraded/recovered policy. No single shared evaluator is established.

reviewed_families.name: extract
reviewed_families.assessment: Extraction mixes provider-specific transcript parsing, cache scope identity and accounting envelopes.
constraints: Claude accepts prebuilt transcript events or item-created notifications; Codex prefers assistant deltas then other events. OpenAI-compatible extraction maps typed events and explicitly skips tool results.
ReadCache.Identity derives root/repository/scoped identities or returns an empty list; it is not a transcript parser.

Claude usage allows cost-only records; Codex thread usage is cumulative and turn usage selects completed or last counters. OpenAI-compatible usage constructs request deltas with attribution and partial-coverage reasons.
DeepSeek, Kimi and OpenRouter already delegate request extraction to a shared adapter. Preserve measurement kind, counter scope, sequence identity and provenance before further consolidation.

reviewed_families.name: failure

constraints: Claude and Codex rate-limit adapters construct nearly identical binding/time envelopes differing in provider and domain failure_reason; a shared envelope constructor is a narrow candidate, not a common reason taxonomy.
Graph.Result preserves calls/pages/rate limit/candidate/diagnostics. PackStatus maps refresh reasons while preserving planning-budget exhaustion. Lifecycle permits atom failures and otherwise nil.
DynamicTool.Response encodes a failure response; OpenAI Tools returns success/output while CommandRunner also includes nil exit_code. Usage validation returns a three-element error tuple.

ProviderMeters.Reconciler preserves ordering by ignoring older or duplicate failure observations while refreshing freshness. Selected BuildOrder UI distinguishes missing versus malformed plans and their status/alert roles.

reviewed_families.name: schedule_tick
reviewed_families.assessment: Bare tick scheduling duplicates an existing helper, but orchestrator scheduling carries cancellation and generation semantics.
constraints: AgentProcessLog, AgentResourceGuard, BuildGateHoldMonitor, RunTelemetry.Sampler and SaturationSentinel directly schedule :tick with no explicit positive-integer guard.

TakeoverAlert.Monitor, Logs.Retention, ProgressCheckin.Worker and PeriodicWorker share the positive-integer guarded :tick form. PeriodicWorker.schedule_tick already exposes the implementation; reuse requires checking callers rather than adding another generic utility.

Read the complete PeriodicWorker module: its macro additionally applies crash isolation, returned-state delay selection and catch-all callbacks. Replacing a timer call does not authorize adopting that full lifecycle policy.

Orchestrator.Lifecycle cancels the prior timer, creates a token and records monotonic due time, allowing zero delay. AwaitingCommands uses a distinct message and fixed module interval. Preserve both distinctions.

reviewed_families.name: truncate

constraints: AgentControlCLI collapses whitespace before shortening. Models, ExecutorListener and RecentMerge reserve one grapheme for the ellipsis; AgentList.Text treats widths at most three without ellipsis.
EventHumanizerHelpers branches on byte_size but slices graphemes and appends three dots; EventRow slices max graphemes then adds an ellipsis. These are not equivalent to a max-total-width contract.

CommandRunner, Opencode.ApiClient and RunTelemetry.Summaries use byte prefixes with different limits and suffixes. Binary cuts may split UTF-8; downstream handling and production incidence remain unverified.

Events.Sanitizer delegates to codepoint_truncate with field-specific limits. Any shared truncation API must explicitly distinguish byte, codepoint, grapheme and display-width policy; none of these clauses establishes terminal cell width.

REPL injection sanitizes text, rejects empty input and sends literal keys then Enter. OpenAI-compatible submission appends user text in Agent state with a request counter and translates session exits.

Orchestrator reconciles send timeouts by message ID and expected content. Dashboard preserves draft and message ID for outcome_unknown, clearing chat only on reported success; API adds an optional nonempty message ID.

CodingAgent, provider wrappers and Orchestrator already delegate across ownership boundaries. A common method name is the adapter contract, not proof of duplicated transport or equivalent completion guarantees.

SessionHandle requires matching schema/backend/hostname and a binary thread ID; invalid handles yield none rather than a validation error. OpenAI-compatible config checks required fields and supported transport.

PriceTable normalizes entries and validates intervals/revisions; ProviderDimensions and Pricing.Dimensions enforce different dimension APIs. Preserve return shapes and failure order; repeated with/case scaffolding is not itself a shared validator.

Webhook controller distinguishes form payload decoding, missing payload, unparsed body and parsed map. StreamDeckGrid retains snapshot freshness and its published timeout/unavailable error codes. No cross-domain payload schema is established.

AdHocSource and OpenTicketSource share DateTime-or-nil validation of now_fun. TicketHistoryProvider instead uses a safe call and falls back to real UTC on invalid/error results.

OpenIssueSnapshot and ResourceStore use system_time; ReadCache, TurnStream and PayloadLoader use monotonic_time; Upgrade uses os_time. Do not compare or substitute these values solely because their units match.

Analytics.Charts chooses window.now_ms or window.end_ms through Map.get; an explicitly present nil differs from a missing key. These wrappers expose domain contracts, not a universal timestamp abstraction.

Asks filters exact open status; Findings selects latest by slug and excludes resolved. DB opening sets busy timeout and closes on pragma failure; that does not establish a read transaction or query-only policy.

TicketContextSelection opens only closed state with valid request epoch, model scope, navigation identity and origin, then rotates request. ContextRuntime adapts socket state; fallbacks preserve state or create an empty selection.

MintSocket includes URI query and defaults absent path to slash; GitHubWebhook exposes a route constant. A generic filesystem helper would be inappropriate for these contracts.

DecisionHistory selects the first available revision from record, answer and revision fields. Any consolidation must preserve precedence and distinguish schema/source contracts from decision revisions. Version parsing bounds and producer behavior are not established by these clauses alone.

reviewed_families.name: normalize_state
reviewed_families.assessment: State normalization spans provider health, GitHub lifecycle, tracker labels and agent mutation authorization.
constraints: The same lifecycle.ex file defines two modules: ProviderHealth accepts health atoms and defaults unavailable, while Lifecycle maps open/closed variants and defaults unknown. These are separate state domains.
Codex TicketState parses a map, strips agent prefix and checks agent-settable states, preserving missing/invalid/unsettable errors. It is more than label normalization.

Membership reconciler and Memory tracker share trimmed lowercase binary normalization with empty-string fallback. GitHub.StatePolicy replaces literal spaces with hyphens; Linear uses a whitespace/underscore regex; Summary.Facts removes separators after normalization and also accepts atoms.
LifecycleFence delegates binary state to DispatchPolicy and otherwise nil. Unifying these helpers without documenting accepted strings and authority scope would change matching or mutation behavior.

reviewed_families.name: notify
reviewed_families.assessment: Notification functions differ in failure isolation, destinations and acceptance evidence.
constraints: Membership and RecentMerge broadcast changes and rescue exceptions. SupervisionHealth also catches exits; DecisionDispatch.Worker catches all kinds and always returns ok after logging callback failure.

DecisionStore separately attempts persisted publication, executor notification and PubSub broadcast; the two shown try blocks rescue exceptions. A successful notify return alone does not prove each downstream delivery.
Realtime audio sends to owner/session directly; TTS checks owner liveness then returns ok. None is an acknowledgment protocol.

Saturation emits distinct central saturated/recovered alerts with different attention/severity. Shared callback mechanics must preserve these policies rather than silently suppressing additional failures.

DecisionAPI first sanitizes then maps public fields/timestamp; DecisionHistory validates JSON-safe DecisionProvenance or returns nil; DecisionSanitizer projects an allowlist. They occupy different trust boundaries.

ModelDiscovery classifies curated-only versus discovered using catalog enablement and fetch timestamp. RunTelemetry.Dataset records input/files/schema versions, first/last timestamps and record count; ordering correctness depends on upstream records.

GitHub Budget computes remaining monotonic command budget, publishes release and returns ok; invalid leases also return ok. Do not equate best-effort release return values with confirmed durable resource removal.

constraints: Tracker and GitHub.Tracker forward to Client, which applies cycle caching. ReviewThreads resolves repository and PR number, consults PollSnapshots, and only on miss calls the live fetch helper.

reviewed_families.name: finish
reviewed_families.assessment: Graph finishing traversals duplicate mechanics; asynchronous finish paths retain ownership checks.
constraints: BuildOrder.Graph and GraphAnalysis perform equivalent visited-set DFS finishing-order traversal, marking a node before recursing through neighbors and prepending it after recursion. This is a narrow algorithm-sharing candidate; callers and overall graph algorithms are not certified equivalent.

CheckpointPersistence accepts completion only when ref and generation match, cancels the timer and clears the pending write; other completions are stale. Refresh distinguishes persistence-required projection from immediate completion and retains waiter/race/full-refresh sequencing.

SourceCollector cancels its timer and kills still-live collection tasks. ElevenLabs closes transport, notifies closure and stops normally. These are different resource lifecycles, not generic completion semantics.

reviewed_families.name: fold

Roster filters summaries, preserves selection and reconciles activity against visible IDs. WarmthIntake distinguishes content, opened panes, visible sessions, started slots, attach state and fully warmed slots; an opened pane is not interchangeable with a warm slot.

UsageAggregate.Projection adds keyed cells, advances source position and generations, and accumulates coverage. Sharing a fold abstraction would not remove the domain-specific ordering and evidence rules.

StatusReason handles atoms recursively, replaces underscores and hyphens without capitalization, and inspects other terms. It supports a different input domain and is not equivalent to the UI formatter.

Common issuance mechanics are a possible scoped investigation, but differing owner selection, registry state and monitoring make replacement unproven. These paths are unrelated to tracker issue projection.

reviewed_families.name: retire
reviewed_families.assessment: Retirement distinguishes authority revocation from ledger watermark advancement.

Tombstones removes the live entry, clears its monitor, forgets continuity, stores the snapshot and maintains a bounded tombstone order. These effects are part of authority lifetime and must remain ordered.

UsageLedger and Store forward a nonnegative watermark retirement request to the owner. This is ledger retention policy, not equivalent to provider binding retirement; durability and downstream compaction behavior are outside this entry-point review.

ModePresenter retains delivery/activity timestamps and polling reasons. DecisionPresenter uses DecisionSanitizer for ticket/source/artifacts/lifecycle/provenance and retains answer revisions and dispatch state.

TicketsPresenter derives routing and search index once per provider read. UnitsRow.Projection joins status/activity/decision/issue facts while preserving replacement boundaries, field sources and health. A generic row helper must not erase those provenance distinctions.

Claude.ReplAgent rejects nonbinary or blank prompts before driving its own turn. OpenAICompat checks the session process, appends user content, runs its loop and commits the turn; invalid/closed sessions have distinct errors.

CodingAgent delegates by session adapter. Further consolidation must preserve pause containment, account notifications, prompt validation and commit behavior, not just equalize signatures. Transitive loops and remote delivery are not verified here.

Existing-atom acceptance is not a domain allowlist: the set depends on loaded atoms. By contrast BuildOrderPresenter only accepts its safe capability reasons.

Aggregate recovery, compaction coordinator and ledger recovery accept atom reasons but use different fallback causes for other terms. Preserve their state/compaction/storage-unavailable distinctions; a shared generic reason must not invent a specific cause.

TicketDetail.Sanitizer validates binary UTF-8 and byte bounds before and after sanitize_base. GithubWebhook.Auth truncates bytes then maps safe log bytes and uses unknown for empty output. These protect different sinks and are not interchangeable.

CurrentRunProjections.SourceAdapter projects run, membership, status, activity, merge and repository shapes. Membership filters nonmap members; activity records degradation when entries are invalid and derives freshness, while status explicitly supplies available/fresh. Those source-specific assumptions require preservation or explicit reconsideration, not a generic sanitize-and-claim-safe helper.
These entry bodies do not establish complete privacy, log safety or source-health correctness; transitive validation and callers remain outside this family check.

OpenAICompat validates the workspace root, resolves configuration, creates an account binding and starts a Session process before binding authority. CodingAgent selects an adapter. BuildOrderTicketContext and TicketContext share underscore-replacement/capitalization for nonnil inputs, but TicketContext adds Unknown for nil. This also overlaps the previously reviewed humanize family and must not be counted as independent savings.

CapacityPresenter describes draining/steady state with an optional maximum. ConversationDrawer distinguishes live, ended, known-empty, stale, unavailable, continuity-unknown, superseded and out-of-scope. Preserve those specific meanings rather than using generic title casing.

Claude.ReplAgent delegates to Reaper. Reaper checks pane identity, invokes group/pane/tree cleanup, observes pane/PID/group disappearance and only unregisters reaper entries on cleanup_proven. This is more than issuing a kill request.

OpenAICompat obtains live session state when possible, stops account generation and the Session process, then returns cleanup_proven; malformed sessions also return that tuple. CodingAgent delegates by session. Do not equate all return values or claim remote cleanup from a shared stop signature; runtime verification remains open.

Claude.HookEvents accepts empty binaries; Usage.Headless.Context trims binaries and converts blank text to nil. Preserve whitespace and empty-value policy explicitly.

UsageEnvelope.ExactMoney maps nil to nil and otherwise calls Atom.to_string: it is an atom serializer, not a binary validator. A universal string_or_nil helper would change accepted input types or errors.

DecisionDelegation serializes policy basis and checks; DecisionProjection carries lifecycle, revision, acknowledgement and resolution structures as well as optional legacy attention/provenance.

Shared atom/time/key conversion mechanics must preserve optional fields and wire compatibility. JSON-safe naming does not prove privacy redaction, semantic validity or safe public disclosure; these serializers expose domain content by design.

RecentMergeStore retains retention/compaction configuration and emits an alert that outcomes are read-only; DeliveryLog retains base state and alerts that deliveries continue without restart-durable deduplication.

UsageLedger recovery resets positions/counter policy and empty coverage while separately marking unavailable health and disabling writes. TicketDetailCoordinator.Policy uses unknown generation and unavailable health.

Tracker and GitHub.Tracker detect three-argument support, fall back to two arguments only for empty options, and otherwise report expected_state_unsupported. Tracker additionally delegates through dispatch_update_issue_state.

CredentialHeadroom returns only a fresh ETS window and maps missing table/key or invalid token key to nil. PriceTable.Validator accepts a fixed flat/peak/off_peak atom/string vocabulary.

ProviderMeters renders exact meters separately from unsupported and supported-but-empty coverage. Analytics.Presenter selects full, active, explicit or trailing-hour intervals; explicit ranges clamp endpoints independently to the full range.

constraints: Claims retains consumers whose renewed_at is strictly later than a time floor, dropping equality.
ReadyForReviewTransitions caps a map by descending PR number, not by timestamp; no change occurs below the cap.
RunTelemetry.Retention delegates to skip_scan? or do_prune, and invalid arguments return ok. Those helpers were not evaluated in this name-family pass.
TicketActivity expires only recent entries strictly older than retention_ms, then applies a recent cap; evictions increment generation and diagnostics. Equality is retained here.
Do not share a retention policy based on this name alone; boundary comparisons, persistent file work and generation effects differ.
